demos.numbered_text:
0 A 6-year-old girl is brought to the physician for a well-child examination.
1 She has no history of serious illness.
2 Her temperature is 37 C (98.6 F), pulse is 95/min, and blood pressure is 96/52 mm
3 Hg.
4 Examination shows a 2/6 continuous, low-pitched murmur over the left upper sternal border that radiates towards the neck.
5 The murmur disappears when she flexes her neck.
6 Suspected of patent ductus arteriosus.
7 The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities.

1 Over the past 9 months, she has had multiple similar episodes of abdominal pain, each lasting for 4â€“5 days.
2 Menarche has not yet occurred.
3 Examination shows suprapubic tenderness to palpation.

0 A 24-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination.
1 She feels well.
2 Menses occur at regular 28-day intervals and last for 3â€“5 days, with normal flow.
3 They are occasionally accompanied by pain.
4 Three years ago, she was diagnosed with chlamydial cervicitis and treated with doxycycline.
5 She has been sexually active with multiple partners since the age of 18 years.
6 She regularly uses condoms for contraception.
7 She drinks 2â€“3 beers on weekends and smokes half a pack of cigarettes daily.
8 Vital signs are within normal limits.
9 Physical examination including a complete pelvic exam shows no abnormalities.
10 A Pap smear shows a low-grade squamous epithelial lesion (LSIL).
11 Patient was recommended a repeat Pap smear in 3 months.

signature.instructions:
You are a physician reviewing a clinical note. The note is either fully correct or contains
exactly one medical error (a wrong diagnosis, management step, treatment, pharmacotherapy or
causal organism). Sentences are numbered from 0. One sentence was selected because it states the
key clinical decision. Decide whether that sentence is medically correct given the rest of the
note. If it is not, rewrite it with the error fixed, keeping the same style.

fields.description: Clinical note, one numbered sentence per line
True if the selected sentence is medically correct
If incorrect, the sentence with the error fixed; if correct, the same sentence
